Security and deployment responsibilities

Review the controls, operating limits, and responsibilities that apply to your facility before using ShorelineOps with resident information.

This page describes product behavior and deployment requirements. It is not a security certification, compliance determination, or service-level agreement.

One facility per deployment

Clinical operations currently require a separate application deployment and database for each facility. Facility identifiers and account roles do not provide complete isolation within a shared clinical database. Switching facility context through a request header is disabled.

Use separate database credentials, signing secrets, backups, and access policies for each installation. A shared multi-facility clinical deployment requires additional isolation work and independent validation.

Accounts and protected actions

The application uses bcrypt password hashing and signed access tokens. Clinical EHR review is limited to dietitian and administrator roles. Purchasing approval and line editing use server-side permission and workflow checks.

Administrators must review user access, configure available multi-factor authentication, and test session expiry on shared devices. An application role does not establish a professional credential.

Clinical decisions and recorded outcomes

Inbound changes require explicit review. Failed requests must remain unresolved until the server confirms the result. Tray verification must use a current signed ticket and available clinical data; unavailable verification requires a hold.

Automated checks support facility procedures. They do not replace authorized clinical orders, physical texture checks, or professional review. Menu assessments without supporting data are shown as not evaluated.

Network outages and recovery

A local SQLite installation can operate without internet while staff remain connected to the local application server. A tablet disconnected from that server cannot verify current orders or confirm saved actions. Browser API responses are not stored in the service-worker cache.

There is no guaranteed offline mutation replay. Prepare a facility-approved downtime procedure, keep required current paper records available, and reconcile recorded outcomes after reconnecting before retrying actions.

Hosting, backups, and audit records

TLS termination, database and backup encryption, retention, monitoring, restore testing, and incident response depend on the chosen hosting configuration. Validate them in the deployed environment; source code alone does not establish these safeguards.

Clinical reconciliation and purchase approval record the authenticated actor with the committed decision. Audit durability and tamper resistance must be tested for the selected database and operating permissions.

Availability commitments, recovery targets, support response times, and any service credits must be established in an executed service agreement. No measured uptime or recovery guarantee is represented here.

Before facility rollout

  • Validate clinical review, tray holds, authorization, and recovery with approved synthetic cases.
  • Test the actual phones, tablets, keyboards, and assistive technology used by staff.
  • Complete a backup restore and network-outage drill.
  • Confirm applicable privacy agreements and responsibilities with the facility and hosting provider.

Report suspected vulnerabilities through the security reporting process in the project repository. Do not include resident information or credentials in public issues.
